summary.en: STATION F is the world's largest startup campus, a 34,000 m² converted railway depot in Paris opened in 2017 with ~€250M of personal investment from billionaire Xavier Niel. It hosts over 1,000 startups and runs 30+ programs; its flagship Founders Program takes a 1% equity stake and writes checks to a small number of startups each year.

strategy.thesis: Iconic private French incubator (2013–early 2020s) that backed digital startups across Paris, London and Berlin, providing support and services in exchange for equity stakes of roughly 1% to 7%.

program.eligibility: Digital-economy startups (program operations largely wound down).

summary.en: The Family was an influential private startup incubator founded in Paris in 2013 by Alice Zagury, Nicolas Colin and Oussama Ammar, taking 1–7% equity in portfolio companies. It worked with hundreds of startups across Paris, London and Berlin, but closed its offices in 2020 and was hit by a 2022 dispute and partial liquidation, making it effectively dormant.

strategy.thesis: Italy's first private venture incubator (founded 2005 by Riccardo Donadon), combining seed investment with incubation services for digital startups; operates as a hybrid VC-and-incubator and now a broader innovation/education ecosystem.

summary.en: H-FARM, founded in 2005 by Riccardo Donadon in Roncade near Treviso, is described as the first private venture incubator in Italy. It combines seed investment with incubation services for digital startups (hybrid VC + incubator), and has grown into a broad innovation and education campus. Its portfolio includes the unicorn Depop.

It has accelerated more than 1,700 companies and is ranked by the Financial Times among the top accelerators in Spain and Portugal.

strategy.thesis: Talent-investment incubator that runs an equity-free 4–6 month program to help vetted founders build companies, then invests up to €100K pre-seed (and up to €500K via partner fund) through its €50M Demium Capital / Think Bigger fund.

summary.en: Demium is a Spanish talent-investment incubator founded in Valencia in 2013. It runs an equity-free 4–6 month program to help founders build companies from idea/talent stage, then invests up to €100K pre-seed (and up to €500K via its partner fund) through the €50M Demium Capital / Think Bigger Fund I. It operates hubs in eight cities across Europe.

summary.en: Founders Foundation is a nonprofit private incubator in Bielefeld, a subsidiary of the Bertelsmann Stiftung, founded by Sebastian Borek, Dominik Gross and the Bertelsmann Stiftung. It promotes B2B-tech entrepreneurship in the East Westphalia-Lippe region through equity-free training and mentoring; 450+ entrepreneurs have taken part and 63 resulting startups have raised over €30M.

summary.en: Startup Wise Guys is an Estonian early-stage accelerator fund founded in Tallinn in 2012, one of the first in the European accelerator scene. Its ~5-month, mostly B2B programs invest up to €100,000 (with follow-on up to €250,000) per startup; the firm has made 400+ investments and 20+ exits across CEE, the Baltics and other 'overlooked' markets.

summary.en: Founders Factory is a London venture studio and accelerator founded in 2015 by Brent Hoberman, Henry Lane Fox and George Northcott. It builds and funds startups in partnership with corporate investors (Aviva, L'Oréal, HSBC, easyJet and others), typically providing around £250K via convertible loan plus operator support for a modest equity stake. It has built/backed 450+ startups across five continents.

summary.en: weXelerate is a Vienna-based multi-corporate accelerator and innovation hub founded in 2016, spanning a ~9,000 m² space in the heart of Vienna. It runs a ~4-month program connecting Austrian and international startups with corporate partners (banking, insurance, industry, energy, media) and takes no equity; its sister program Venturecake is described as Austria's first co-owned accelerator.

summary.en: Factory Berlin is a membership-based private startup campus and community founded in 2012, housing startups and corporates across two Berlin campuses. Unlike equity-taking incubators, it charges a membership fee ('organic acceleration') and provides workspace, mentorship and corporate/investor access; it has scaled back, closing its main location, so it is treated as dormant.
